original_value: Hashing method is an efficient technique of multimedia security for content protection. It maps an image into a content-based compact code for denoting the image itself. While most existing algorithms focus on improving the classification between robustness and discrimination, little attention has been paid to geometric invariance under normal digital operations, and therefore results in quite fragile to geometric distortion when applied in image copy detection. In this article, a novel effective image hashing method is proposed based on geometric invariant vector distance in both spatial domain and frequency domain. First, the image is preprocessed by some joint operations to extract robust features. Then, the preprocessed image is randomly divided into several overlapping blocks under a secret key, and two different feature matrices are separately obtained in the spatial domain and frequency domain through invariant moment and low frequency discrete cosine transform coefficients. Furthermore, the invariant distances between vectors in feature matrices are calculated and quantified to form a compact hash code. We conduct various experiments to demonstrate that the proposed hashing not only reaches good classification between robustness and discrimination, but also resists most geometric distortion in image copy detection. In addition, both receiver operating characteristics curve comparisons and mean average precision in copy detection clearly illustrate that the proposed hashing method outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms.

result.paraphrase: Hashing is an efficient multimedia security technique for content protection. It converts an image into a compact content-based code that represents the image itself. Although most existing methods emphasize the tradeoff between robustness and discrimination, they pay little attention to geometric invariance under ordinary digital operations, leaving image copy detection results highly vulnerable to geometric distortion. This paper proposes a novel and effective image hashing method based on geometric-invariant vector distance in both the spatial and frequency domains. First, the image undergoes joint preprocessing operations to extract robust features. Next, under a secret key, the preprocessed image is randomly split into several overlapping blocks, and two distinct feature matrices are extracted separately in the spatial domain and frequency domain using invariant moments and low-frequency discrete cosine transform coefficients. In addition, invariant distances between vectors in the feature matrices are computed and quantized to produce a compact hash code. Experimental results show that the proposed hashing method achieves a good balance between robustness and discrimination while also resisting most geometric distortions in image copy detection. Receiver operating characteristic curve comparisons and mean average precision results further show that it outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms in copy detection.
